# NodePaint

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

What an element paints, captured so the compliance preflight can evaluate colour contrast (`../Compliance/ComplianceEvaluator`) without a second render pass or any inspection of the rendered output.

Colours are `"#rrggbb"` strings with alpha carried separately, so an opaque document produces no alpha fields at all and fixtures stay readable across languages. Nodes that paint nothing relevant omit `paint` entirely.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

## Properties

- [`backdropUnknown`](#backdropunknown): The node paints something behind its children that cannot be reduced to one opaque colour — a background *element* rather than a colour, layers, a gradient, or a drawing surface.
- [`background`](#background): The element's own resolved background fill, `"#rrggbb"`.
- [`backgroundAlpha`](#backgroundalpha): Background alpha in `[0,1)`; omitted when fully opaque.
- [`bold`](#bold): True when the resolved font weight is 700 or heavier.
- [`fontSize`](#fontsize): Rendered text size in points.
- [`text`](#text): Resolved text colour, `"#rrggbb"`.
- [`textAlpha`](#textalpha): Text alpha in `[0,1)`; omitted when fully opaque.
- [`textBackdrop`](#textbackdrop): An opaque backdrop resolved from earlier drawing operations in the same canvas.

### `backdropUnknown`

```typescript
backdropUnknown?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

The node paints something behind its children that cannot be reduced to one opaque colour — a background *element* rather than a colour, layers, a gradient, or a drawing surface. Descendant text is reported as `contrast-unknown` rather than measured against a guess.
